sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%无形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Neil Young is a rare artiSt.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·杨是一位罕见的艺术家。

sentences.en: He's had big commercial success while also enjoying credibility as a musician's musician.
sentences.zh: 他在商业上取得了巨大成功，同时也作为音乐人中的音乐人赢得了声誉。

sentences.en: He's also insanely prolific.
sentences.zh: 而且他的创作力极其旺盛。

sentences.en: Young has released dozens of albuMs.
sentences.zh: 杨发行了数十张专辑。

sentences.en: It's hard to pick a favorite Neil Young song, but I'm a simple man, and I think mine is probably Harvest Moon.
sentences.zh: 很难挑选出最喜欢的尼尔·杨歌曲，但我是一个简单的人，我想我的最爱大概是《丰收月》吧。

sentences.en: Look, there are a lot of great choices.
sentences.zh: 听着，有很多伟大的选择。

sentences.en: I think I'm more of a heart of gold guy myself.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我更偏爱《金心》这首歌。

sentences.en: But Neil Young is not just some legend of classic rock.
sentences.zh: 但尼尔·杨不仅仅是什么经典摇滚传奇。

sentences.en: Best producer, Chris Berube.
sentences.zh: 最佳制作人，克里斯·贝鲁比。

sentences.en: There is a whole other side of Neil Young's career, his bizarre experimental side.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·杨的职业生涯还有完全不同的另一面，他那古怪的实验性一面。

sentences.en: There's the Neil Young who made a divisive electronic music album.
sentences.zh: 有制作了备受争议的电子音乐专辑的尼尔·杨。

sentences.en: Or the Neil Young who designs model train sets.
sentences.zh: 还有设计模型火车的尼尔·杨。

sentences.en: Neil Young even directed a very confusing sci-fi movie in the 80s starring Devo.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·杨甚至在80年代执导了一部由迪沃乐队主演、让人一头雾水的科幻电影。

sentences.en: It's called Human Highway.
sentences.zh: 它叫《人类高速公路》。

sentences.en: Good gas!
sentences.zh: 好汽油！

sentences.en: Oh, it's bird gas.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是鸟的屁。

sentences.en: It's the beSt.
sentences.zh: 这是最棒的。

sentences.en: You make it yourself?
sentences.zh: 你自己做的？

sentences.en: No, it's come from bird.
sentences.zh: 不，这是鸟拉的。

sentences.en: Human Highway, man.
sentences.zh: 《人类高速公路》，老兄。

sentences.en: It's a weird one.
sentences.zh: 这是一部很诡异的作品。

sentences.en: But perhaps the biggest swing came about four decades into his career,
sentences.zh: 但也许他职业生涯中最大胆的一次尝试出现在大约四十年后，

sentences.en: when Neil Young decided to make his own digital music player, which he called the Pono.
sentences.zh: 当时尼尔·杨决定打造自己的数字音乐播放器，他将其命名为Pono。

sentences.en: You don't like the iTunes and the iPod and that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你不喜欢iTunes、iPod以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: You've got this thing called Pono, which is your own music player.
sentences.zh: 你搞了这个叫Pono的东西，它是你自己的音乐播放器。

sentences.en: Well, because it's not that I don't like it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为倒不是说我不喜欢它。

sentences.en: It's just I can't play what I do.
sentences.zh: 只是我没法播放我创作的东西。

sentences.en: The Pono was meant to be a competitor to the iPod.
sentences.zh: Pono本意是作为iPod的竞争对手出现的。

sentences.en: The Pono was a portable digital music player.
sentences.zh: Pono是一款便携式数字音乐播放器。

sentences.en: But unlike the iPod, it had a long, triangular, candy bar-esque shape.
sentences.zh: 但与iPod不同，它有着修长、呈三角形、类似巧克力的外观。

sentences.en: It's not a, it looks like a Toblerone.
sentences.zh: 它不是，它看起来像个三角巧克力。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 它不是。

sentences.en: It doesn't taste.
sentences.zh: 它没有味道。

sentences.en: What is this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么？

sentences.en: For your ears, it's even better than a Toblerone.
sentences.zh: 为了你的耳朵，它甚至比三角巧克力还要好。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it sounds.
sentences.zh: 是的，听起来就是这样。

sentences.en: Have you ever jammed a Toblerone in your ear, my friend?
sentences.zh: 我的朋友，你往耳朵里塞过三角巧克力吗？

sentences.en: Neil Young unleashed the Pono in 2015 with a lot of media coverage and endorsements from famous musicians like Bruce Springsteen and Tom Petty.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·杨在2015年推出了Pono，伴随着大量的媒体报道以及布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀和汤姆·佩蒂等著名音乐人的背书。

sentences.en: But the Toblerone-esque music player was confusing to a lot of potential consumers.
sentences.zh: 但这个三角巧克力造型的音乐播放器让许多潜在消费者感到困惑。

sentences.en: Most people just didn't understand why it was necessary to replace their iPods with another device that retailed for about $400.
sentences.zh: 大多数人根本不理解，为什么非得用另一款售价约400美元的设备来取代他们的iPod。

sentences.en: Even Neil Young's fans did not totally get it.
sentences.zh: 甚至连尼尔·杨的粉丝也没有完全搞懂。

sentences.en: My initial reaction to it was really just sort of like, eh, let's see, I was 25 when it came out.
sentences.zh: 我对它的最初反应其实就是，呃，看看吧，它问世时我25岁。

sentences.en: I didn't have a lot of expendable income at that point.
sentences.zh: 那时候我没有多少可支配收入。

sentences.en: I wasn't in the market for something to replace my iPod.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不急着找个东西来替换我的iPod。

sentences.en: That's Nate Rogers, a writer and a music critic who wrote about Pono for the website Stereo Gum earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 那是内特·罗杰斯，一位作家兼音乐评论家，今年早些时候他曾在Stereo Gum网站上撰文谈论过Pono。

sentences.en: Nate also happens to be a Neil Young super fan.
sentences.zh: 内特碰巧也是尼尔·杨的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: I have a Neil Young, a picture of Neil Young on the wall in here that I've been looking.
sentences.zh: 我这里有一张尼尔·杨的照片，贴在墙上，我一直在看。

sentences.en: I'm sitting directly across from 1979.
sentences.zh: 我正对面的就是1979年的照片。

sentences.en: It's Russ Never Sleeps tour.
sentences.zh: 那是他的“锈迹不眠”巡演。

sentences.en: He's really rocking out with Crazy Horse.
sentences.zh: 他和疯马乐队一起摇滚得十分尽兴。

sentences.en: Looks happy.
sentences.zh: 看起来很高兴。

sentences.en: If you've never heard of Pono before, that's because it came and went in a few short years.
sentences.zh: 如果你以前从没听说过Pono，那是因为它仅仅存在了短短几年就昙花一现了。

sentences.en: And at the time, many critics dismissed Pono as a celebrity vanity project.
sentences.zh: 当时，许多评论家把Pono斥为名人的虚荣项目。

sentences.en: But reading Nate Rogers' piece made me wonder if we were wrong about Pono.
sentences.zh: 但读了内特·罗杰斯的文章后，我开始怀疑我们是不是误解了Pono。

sentences.en: Because Nate's article is actually headlined,
sentences.zh: 因为内特的文章标题其实是：

sentences.en: What if we were wrong about Pono?
sentences.zh: 如果我们对Pono的看法是错的呢？

sentences.en: In the early 2010s, Neil Young was enjoying something of a career resurgence.
sentences.zh: 在2010年代初，尼尔·杨的职业生涯迎来了某种复苏。

sentences.en: He was playing shows across North America with his band Crazy Horse, and he was getting some of the best reviews of his career.
sentences.zh: 他带着他的疯马乐队在北美各地演出，并获得了他职业生涯中一些最好的评价。

sentences.en: But in interviews, Neil seemed upset, almost angry.
sentences.zh: 但在采访中，尼尔看起来很不高兴，甚至有点愤怒。

sentences.en: He told journalists he was unhappy with the rise of digital downloads, and that he didn't want to listen to songs on a computer.
sentences.zh: 他告诉记者，他对数字下载的兴起感到不满，他不想在电脑上听歌。

sentences.en: In fact, in one interview, Neil Young claimed he hadn't listened to music for over 15 years.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在一次采访中，尼尔·杨声称他已经有15年多没听过音乐了。

sentences.en: I don't know how it's possible to not listen to music for 15 years, even if you're not a musician.
sentences.zh: 我不知道15年不听音乐怎么可能做到，即使你不是音乐人。

sentences.en: So, I don't really know what Neil was talking about there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我其实不太懂尼尔当时在说什么。

sentences.en: I feel like he meant to say, like, I haven't listened to digital music in 15 years.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他的意思是想说，比如，我15年没听过数字音乐了。

sentences.en: But he did say that, so whatever, maybe he did.
sentences.zh: 但他确实是那样说的，所以管他呢，也许他真的没听吧。

sentences.en: Neil is an interesting person.
sentences.zh: 尼尔是一个有趣的人。

sentences.en: Um, love him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，爱死他了。

sentences.en: You're probably thinking this all sounds like typical old guy, back in my day, stuff was better, kind of crankiness.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得这一切听起来就像是典型的老头子那种“想当年，以前的东西更好”的牢骚怪脾气。

sentences.en: And to be fair, yes, okay, maybe it's a little bit of that.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，是的，好吧，也许确实有点那种意思。

sentences.en: But Neil Young actually had a good reason for boycotting digital music.
sentences.zh: 但尼尔·杨抵制数字音乐其实有充分的理由。

sentences.en: According to Young, digitized music just sounded wrong.
sentences.zh: 在杨看来，数字化音乐听起来就是不对劲。

sentences.en: The origin of the Pono is that Neil Young thinks that digital music destroyed music quality in general.
sentences.zh: Pono的由来是尼尔·杨认为数字音乐总体上摧毁了音乐的质量。

sentences.en: When Neil got his start in the 60s, everybody was listening to music on vinyl.
sentences.zh: 当尼尔在60年代出道时，每个人都在听黑胶唱片。

sentences.en: Today, of course, lots of folks love vinyl, but vinyl records were delicate and not super mobile.
sentences.zh: 当然，如今许多人都喜欢黑胶唱片，但黑胶唱片很脆弱，而且很不方便携带。

sentences.en: So, in the 80s and 90s, vinyl was pushed out by new formats, like cassette tapes and CDs.
sentences.zh: 所以，在80和90年代，黑胶唱片被卡式磁带和CD等新格式挤出了市场。

sentences.en: Cassettes were portable and handy.
sentences.zh: 磁带便携又实用。

sentences.en: You could pop one of those bad boys into your Walkman or the console of your Dodge Neon and hit the road.
sentences.zh: 你可以把其中一个宝贝塞进你的随身听或者道奇霓虹汽车的中控台，然后上路。

sentences.en: But in the 90s, cassettes lost the format wars to CDs, which were slim and futuristic.
sentences.zh: 但在90年代，磁带在格式之战中输给了纤薄且具有未来感的CD。

sentences.en: They were just as portable as cassettes, but sounded much better.
sentences.zh: 它们和磁带一样便携，但听起来好得多。

sentences.en: They didn't wear out or scratch as easily as vinyl.
sentences.zh: 它们不像黑胶那样容易磨损或刮花。

sentences.en: And they were free of the noise that plagued analog formats.
sentences.zh: 并且没有困扰模拟格式的噪音。

sentences.en: But to people like Neil Young, there was something lost with the rise of CDs.
sentences.zh: 但在尼尔·杨这样的人看来，随着CD的兴起，有些东西丢失了。

sentences.en: A warmth.
sentences.zh: 一种温暖感。

sentences.en: And MP3s?
sentences.zh: 还有MP3？

sentences.en: Well, that's where things started to get a whole lot worse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事情就是从这里开始变得更糟糕的。

sentences.en: Because of something called compression.
sentences.zh: 因为一种叫做压缩的东西。

sentences.en: Basically, to fit a lot of songs onto a hard drive or an iPod, the files had to be pretty small.
sentences.zh: 基本上，为了把大量歌曲塞进硬盘或iPod，文件必须做得很小。

sentences.en: Which means they had to be compressed or squeezed down in a way that reduces the quality of the music you're listening to.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们必须经过压缩或挤压，这会降低你所听音乐的质量。

sentences.en: I guess the term is probably appropriately decimated.
sentences.zh: 我想这个词用“惨遭摧毁”来形容大概很贴切。

sentences.en: Maybe a tenth of that CD makes it onto an MP3 file.
sentences.zh: 一张CD里大概只有十分之一的内容能进入MP3文件。

sentences.en: A way of measuring sound quality on a digital music file is in kilobits per second.
sentences.zh: 衡量数字音乐文件音质的一种方法是千比特每秒。

sentences.en: A music file on a CD has about 1,400 kilobits of information per second.
sentences.zh: CD上的音乐文件每秒包含约1400千比特的信息。

sentences.en: In a streaming MP3, that number goes down to about 96.
sentences.zh: 在流媒体MP3中，这个数字下降到了大约96。

sentences.en: It's shocking, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这令人震惊。

sentences.en: It's very significant.
sentences.zh: 这是非常显著的差距。

sentences.en: It's hard to explain what gets lost when you do that much compression on an audio file.
sentences.zh: 很难解释当你对音频文件进行如此大程度的压缩时，到底丢失了什么。

sentences.en: An MP3 of a song and a vinyl record might sound pretty similar to untrained ears.
sentences.zh: 对于未经训练的耳朵来说，一首歌的MP3和黑胶唱片听起来可能差不太多。

sentences.en: But to trained ears, there's a real difference.
sentences.zh: 但对受过专业训练的耳朵来说，有着真正的区别。

sentences.en: You know, a sense of ease to the sound.
sentences.zh: 你知道，声音有一种轻松感。

sentences.en: And that's going to be subjective and individual.
sentences.zh: 而这因人而异，具有主观性。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, you know, if you listen to MP3s seriously, your attention wanders.
sentences.zh: 不过尽管如此，你知道的，如果你认真听MP3，你的注意力就会分散。

sentences.en: John Atkinson is the former editor of Stereophile magazine.
sentences.zh: 约翰·阿特金森是《发烧友》杂志的前主编。

sentences.en: He says that with MP3s, listeners actually lose something pretty fundamental.
sentences.zh: 他说，听MP3时，听众实际上失去了一些非常基础的东西。

sentences.en: Any transients in the music, you know, cymbal crashes, beats, druMs.
sentences.zh: 音乐中的任何瞬态音，你知道的，镲片撞击声、节拍、鼓声。

sentences.en: So what was a clean hit on a drum now becomes more of a burr on a drum.
sentences.zh: 所以原本在鼓上清脆的一击，现在变成了一种类似鼓面带刺的粗糙声音。

sentences.en: So if you listen to low-res MP3s, you start to aware that the sense of rhythm has been degraded.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你听低分辨率的MP3，你开始意识到节奏感已经退化了。

sentences.en: You're missing a lot of the harmonics when you strum a guitar or hit a piano key.
sentences.zh: 当你扫吉他或按钢琴键时，你丢失了很大一部分泛音。

sentences.en: You hear one note, but you also hear a whole series of harmonics and notes that trail off.
sentences.zh: 你听到了一个音符，但也听到了一连串渐行渐远的泛音和音符。

sentences.en: That's Phil Baker.
sentences.zh: 那是菲尔·贝克。

sentences.en: He worked as the product manager for Pono starting in 2012.
sentences.zh: 他从2012年开始担任Pono的产品经理。

sentences.en: You know, when you strum a guitar string, it's not just boom.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你拨动吉他弦时，它不只是“砰”的一声。

sentences.en: It's ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba.
sentences.zh: 而是“叭叭叭叭叭叭叭叭叭叭叭”。

sentences.en: So all those other things are lost, or a good number of them are lost, because it's just truncates.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些其他东西都丢失了，或者其中很大一部分丢失了，因为它是直接被截断的。

sentences.en: It doesn't have the ability to play back that fine detail.
sentences.zh: 它没有能力播放出那种细腻的细节。

sentences.en: There are a lot of subtleties.
sentences.zh: 有很多微妙之处。

sentences.en: For many people, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，这没关系。

sentences.en: They hear a music they're used to listening to radio, whether it's AM or FM or Sirius XM, which, by the way, you know, transmits in a very, very low resolution.
sentences.zh: 他们习惯了听广播里的音乐，无论是AM、FM还是天狼星卫星广播，顺便说一句，你知道的，它的传输分辨率非常非常低。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Thanks, Phil.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，菲尔。

sentences.en: When MP3s became the dominant way of listening to music, a lot of casual listeners just didn't mind the tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 当MP3成为听音乐的主导方式时，许多普通听众并不介意这种妥协。

sentences.en: But Neil Young believed he could do better.
sentences.zh: 但尼尔·杨相信他能做得更好。

sentences.en: Because he had unbelievable resources, and because he's a very, very stubborn man, he was like, I'll just do it myself.
sentences.zh: 因为他拥有难以置信的资源，而且他是一个非常非常固执的人，他当时想，我自己来做好了。

sentences.en: And that's where Pono came from.
sentences.zh: Pono就是这样诞生的。

sentences.en: In 2012, Neil Young announced his plans for the Pono player.
sentences.zh: 2012年，尼尔·杨公布了他的Pono播放器计划。

sentences.en: To give listeners a truly great experience, he devised a plan for an online store that would only sell high-quality music files.
sentences.zh: 为了给听众提供真正极佳的体验，他制定了一个计划：建立一个只出售高质量音乐文件的在线商店。

sentences.en: Neil said Pono files wouldn't be comparable to what you would get on a record, but they would be a lot better than an MP3.
sentences.zh: 尼尔说，Pono的文件无法与你在唱片上听到的相比，但它们会比MP3好得多。

sentences.en: While this whole thing is pretty technical, Neil made a handy video using a nautical metaphor to explain it.
sentences.zh: 虽然整件事非常技术化，但尼尔用了一个巧妙的航海隐喻来解释它。

sentences.en: When you're on the bottom of the ocean, and you have a huge tank on your back and a big glass ball over your head,
sentences.zh: 当你在海底，背上背着一个巨大的气罐，头上套着一个大玻璃球，

sentences.en: that's kind of, you know, you're walking around in the murk and there's big fish down there.
sentences.zh: 这就有点像，你知道的，你在浑浊的水中走动，大鱼就在下面游来游去。

sentences.en: That's kind of like listening to an MP3.
sentences.zh: 这有点像听MP3。

sentences.en: And when you're listening to a CD, you've risen to, you know, maybe a couple hundred feet below the surface, something like that.
sentences.zh: 而当你听CD时，你已经上升到了离水面大约几百英尺的地方，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And you're still underwater.
sentences.zh: 你仍然在水下。

sentences.en: You're not quite in air.
sentences.zh: 你还没完全浮出水面。

sentences.en: And according to Neil, to get to air, figuratively speaking, you need some Pono.
sentences.zh: 按照尼尔的说法，要浮到空气中，比喻意义上讲，你需要一些Pono。

sentences.en: And the feeling is different.
sentences.zh: 而且感觉是不一样的。

sentences.en: Actually is a visceral relief.
sentences.zh: 实际上是一种发自内心的解脱。

sentences.en: You feel good.
sentences.zh: 你感觉很好。

sentences.en: With the store, listeners could buy higher-quality files without going through a big tech middleman.
sentences.zh: 有了这家商店，听众无需通过大型科技中间商就能买到更高质量的文件。

sentences.en: Each album would cost about 20 bucks, which was higher than iTunes,
sentences.zh: 每张专辑售价约20美元，比iTunes要高，

sentences.en: but musicians would be paid more than the pennies they were getting from Apple.
sentences.zh: 但音乐人获得的报酬将比他们从苹果那里拿到的几分钱要多。
